items.title: 4.5 Adjoint and Inverse of a Square Matrix (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Aaj ka sabaq is unit ka ek bohat aham hissa hai: matrix ka inverse. Numbers mein aap jaante hain ke 5 ka inverse \(\frac{1}{5}\) hai, kyun ke \(5 \times \frac{1}{5} = 1\). Matrices mein "1" ka kaam identity matrix \(I\) karta hai. To \(A\) ka inverse \(A^{-1}\) woh matrix hai jis se \(A\) ko multiply karein to \(I\) mile. Is ko banane ke liye humein wahi cofactors chahiye jo 4.4.1 mein seekhe the. Dekhiye, pichli saari mehnat yahan kaam aa rahi hai.
to \(A\) ke cofactors ka matrix (har element ki jagah us ka cofactor) yeh hai:
\[\operatorname{adj} A = \begin{bmatrix} A_{11} & A_{21} & A_{31} \\ A_{12} & A_{22} & A_{32} \\ A_{13} & A_{23} & A_{33} \end{bmatrix}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Dono matrices ko ghor se milayein: \(\operatorname{adj} A\) (\(A\) ka adjoint) cofactors ke matrix ka transpose hai. \(A\) ki row 1 ke cofactors \(\operatorname{adj} A\) ke column 1 mein khare hain, row 2 ke cofactors column 2 mein, aur row 3 ke column 3 mein. Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: "cofactors nikaalo, phir letaa do (rows ko columns bana do)".
Inverse of a Square Matrix of Order n ≥ 3

Kitab ki definition: maan lijiye \(A\) order \(n\) ka non-singular square matrix hai, yani \(|A| \ne 0\). Agar koi matrix \(B\) aisa ho ke \(AB = BA = I_{n}\), to \(B\) ko \(A\) ka multiplicative inverse kehte hain aur \(A^{-1}\) likhte hain. Zahir hai ke \(A^{-1}\) ka order bhi \(n \times n\) hoga, warna \(AB\) aur \(BA\) dono ban hi nahin sakte.
Yani \(AA^{-1} = I_{n}\) aur \(A^{-1}A = I_{n}\).
Agar \(A\) non-singular ho to

blocks.text_alt: A inverse equals one over the determinant of A, times adjoint of A

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh formula kaam kyun karta hai? \(A\) ko \(\operatorname{adj} A\) se multiply karke dekhiye. Diagonal ki har entry = \(A\) ki ek row \(\times\) usi row ke cofactors, jo bilkul \(|A|\) ki expansion hai. Diagonal se bahar ki har entry = ek row \(\times\) kisi doosri row ke cofactors, jo aise determinant ki expansion hai jis ki do rows ek jaisi hain, is liye 0 (property iii). Natija:
\[A(\operatorname{adj} A) = |A|\,I\]
Ab dono taraf \(|A|\) se divide karein to \(A\left(\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A\right) = I\). Yani \(\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A\) hi \(A^{-1}\) hai.
Isi liye \(|A| \ne 0\) zaroori hai: zero se divide nahin ho sakta. Jis matrix ka \(|A| = 0\) ho use singular kehte hain, aur us ka koi inverse nahin hota, bilkul jaise number 0 ka koi inverse nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Order 3 ka inverse nikalne ke qadam (yeh tarteeb yaad kar lein):
1. Pehle \(|A|\) nikaalein. Agar 0 aaye to ruk jayein: inverse nahin hai.
2. Nau ke nau (9) cofactors \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\) nikaalein.
3. Cofactors ka matrix likhein aur us ka transpose lein: yeh \(\operatorname{adj} A\) hai.
4. \(\operatorname{adj} A\) ki har entry ko \(|A|\) se divide karein.
5. Tasdeeq: \(AA^{-1} = I\) aana chahiye.

Ab kitab ki Example 7 inhi qadmon par chalti hai. Kitab ke scan mein do cofactors, \(A_{23}\) aur \(A_{32}\), ke label aur power dhundle chhape hain; hum ne unhein khud derive kiya hai (misaal ke baad wazahat dekhiye).

blocks.title: Example 7
steps:
Given: \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\).
To find: \(A^{-1}\).
Method: sab se pehle formula yaad karte hain: \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A\). Is ke liye teen cheezein chahiye: (1) nau ke nau (9) cofactors, (2) \(\operatorname{adj} A\), yani cofactors ke matrix ka transpose, (3) \(|A|\), jo zero nahin hona chahiye. Hum isi tarteeb se chalenge.

Step 1: Row 1 ke cofactors
\[A_{11} = (-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(2 + 1) = 3\]
\[A_{12} = (-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(-1) = 1\]
\[A_{13} = (-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(0 - 2) = -2\]
Kyun: \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\); har minor \(A\) ki row \(i\) aur column \(j\) mita kar milta hai. \(A_{11}\) mein \(ad - bc = 2(1) - 1(-1) = 3\); yahan double minus plus ban gaya.

Step 2: Row 2 ke cofactors
\[A_{21} = (-1)^{2+1}\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(0 + 2) = -2\]
\[A_{22} = (-1)^{2+2}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(1 - 2) = -1\]
\[A_{23} = (-1)^{2+3}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(-1 - 0) = 1\]
Kyun: wahi rule. \(A_{23}\) ke liye row 2 aur column 3 mitayein; \(1, 0, 1, -1\) bachte hain, minor \(= -1 - 0 = -1\). \(2 + 3 = 5\) odd hai, is liye sign ulta: \(A_{23} = 1\).
Dhyan dein: kitab ke scan mein \(A_{23}\) ka label aur power dhundle chhape hain; hum ne label aur power khud derive kar ke likhe hain.

Step 3: Row 3 ke cofactors
\[A_{31} = (-1)^{3+1}\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(0 - 4) = -4\]
\[A_{32} = (-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(1 - 0) = -1\]
\[A_{33} = (-1)^{3+3}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(2 - 0) = 2\]
Kyun: wahi rule. \(A_{32}\) ke liye row 3 aur column 2 mitayein; \(1, 2, 0, 1\) bachte hain, minor \(= 1 - 0 = 1\). \(3 + 2 = 5\) odd, is liye \(A_{32} = -1\). (Kitab mein is ka label bhi dhundla hai.)

Step 4: Cofactors ka matrix aur us ka transpose
\[[A_{ij}]_{3 \times 3} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ -4 & -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[\operatorname{adj} A = [A'_{ij}]_{3 \times 3}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 & -4 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\operatorname{adj} A\) cofactors ke matrix ka transpose hai (\(A'_{ij} = A_{ji}\)): pehli row \(3, 1, -2\) pehla column ban jati hai, doosri row doosra column, waghera. Yeh transpose wala qadam bhoolna sab se aam ghalti hai.

Step 5: Determinant
\[|A| = a_{11}A_{11} + a_{12}A_{12} + a_{13}A_{13}\]
\[= 1(3) + 0(1) + 2(-2)\]
\[= 3 + 0 - 4 = -1\]
Kyun: row 1 ke cofactors pehle hi nikal chuke hain, is liye row 1 se kholna sab se aasan hai (aur \(a_{12} = 0\) ki wajah se ek term khud hi zero). \(|A| = -1 \ne 0\), yani \(A\) non-singular hai aur \(A^{-1}\) maujood hai. Agar yahan 0 aata to sawal yahin khatam: inverse hota hi nahin.

Step 6: Inverse
\[A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{-1}\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 & -4 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 & 4 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{-1} = -1\), is liye \(\operatorname{adj} A\) ki har entry ka sign ulta ho gaya.

Tasdeeq:
Ab dekhte hain ke jawab sach mein sahi hai ya nahin: \(A\) ko \(A^{-1}\) se multiply karein to identity matrix aana chahiye.
\[AA^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[\times \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 & 4 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\]
Row 1 (columns ke saath): \(-3 + 0 + 4 = 1\), \(2 + 0 - 2 = 0\), \(4 + 0 - 4 = 0\)
Row 2: \(0 - 2 + 2 = 0\), \(0 + 2 - 1 = 1\), \(0 + 2 - 2 = 0\)
Row 3: \(-3 + 1 + 2 = 0\), \(2 - 1 - 1 = 0\), \(4 - 1 - 2 = 1\)
\[AA^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = I_{3}\]
Product identity matrix hai, is liye inverse bilkul sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 7 mein do cofactors ke label saaf nahin chhape: ek \(A_{3} = (-1)^{2+}\dots\) jaisa aur doosra \(A_{2} = (-1)^{3\,2}\dots\) jaisa dikhta hai. Un ki jagah aur minors se saaf hai ke yeh
\(A_{23} = (-1)^{2+3}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = (-1)(-1 - 0) = 1\) aur
\(A_{32} = (-1)^{3+2}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = (-1)(1 - 0) = -1\) hain.
Kitab ki values 1 aur \(-1\) sahi hain, aur aakhri \(A^{-1}\) bhi sahi hai.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text:
Exam mein waqt bachane ka ek tareeqa: \(|A|\) ke liye alag se poora determinant mat kholiye. Cofactors to aap pehle hi nikal chuke hain, bas kisi ek row ke elements ko unhi ke cofactors se multiply kar ke jama kar dein, jaise Example 7 ke Step 5 mein kiya. Lekin agar \(|A|\) zero aane ka shak ho, to behtar hai ke sab se pehle \(|A|\) hi nikaal lein; zero aaye to baqi cofactors nikaalne ki zaroorat hi nahin.
Doosri baat: aakhri jawab mein fraction ko matrix ke andar le jana zaroori nahin. \(\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix} \dots \end{bmatrix}\) bhi bilkul sahi jawab hai. Yahan \(|A| = -1\) tha, is liye andar le jana aasan tha.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Example 7 mein \(A(\operatorname{adj} A)\) kya hoga, bina poora multiply kiye?
Jawab: \(A(\operatorname{adj} A) = |A|\,I = -I\), yani diagonal par \(-1\) aur baqi sab 0. Chahein to multiply kar ke check kar lein.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin. \(F = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) ka inverse.
\(|F|\): row 3 se kholein (do zeros): \(|F| = 1 \cdot (2 - 1) = 1\).
Cofactors: \(F_{11} = 1\), \(F_{12} = -1\), \(F_{13} = 0\), \(F_{21} = -1\), \(F_{22} = 2\), \(F_{23} = 0\), \(F_{31} = 0\), \(F_{32} = 0\), \(F_{33} = 1\).
Transpose karne par \(\operatorname{adj} F = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), aur \(|F| = 1\) hai, is liye \(F^{-1} = \operatorname{adj} F\).
Tasdeeq: \(F F^{-1}\) ki pehli row: \(2 - 1 = 1\), \(-2 + 2 = 0\), \(0\). Baqi rows bhi isi tarah \(I\) deti hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Cofactors ka matrix: har element ki jagah us ka cofactor.
2. \(\operatorname{adj} A\) = cofactors ke matrix ka transpose.
3. \(A^{-1}\) sirf tab hai jab \(|A| \ne 0\) (non-singular matrix).
4. \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj} A\), aur \(AA^{-1} = A^{-1}A = I\).
5. \(A(\operatorname{adj} A) = |A|\,I\); Example 7 mein yeh \(-I\) hai.
6. Jawab hamesha \(A\) aur \(A^{-1}\) ko multiply kar ke check karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Transpose bhool jana: cofactors ka matrix khud \(\operatorname{adj} A\) NAHIN hai. Bachne ka tareeqa: "row ke cofactors, column mein".
2. Signs \((-1)^{i+j}\) bhool kar minors hi likh dena.
3. \(|A| = 0\) hone par bhi divide kar dena: singular matrix ka inverse hota hi nahin.
4. \(\operatorname{adj} A\) ki sirf kuch entries ko \(|A|\) se divide karna: har entry divide hoti hai.
5. \(A^{-1} = \frac{1}{A}\) likh dena: matrix se divide karna defined hi nahin.
